title: Support of an orthogonal vector
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a set of coordinates among $n$ coordinates, and let $\gamma\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$ be orthogonal under the standard dot product to every vector that vanishes on $S$. Then every coordinate where $\gamma$ is nonzero belongs to $S$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite set $S$ of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates
Vector $\gamma\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$ belongs to the orthogonal complement of the subspace of vectors vanishing on $S$
